title: Who wrote what
hookLine: scholars debate the authorship of some letters; churches receive them all as scripture
tomorrow: why do some lines in Paul's letters suddenly sound like a song?

lines: I TERTIUS, WHO WROTE THIS EPISTLE.
cards: A grandmother's hands shake too much to type, so she talks and her granddaughter types. Tell your uncle the roses came up. At the bottom, before sending, the granddaughter slips in a line of her own: hi, it's me typing.
Near the end of Romans, the very same thing happens. In the middle of Paul's greetings, a new voice breaks in: "I Tertius, who wrote this epistle, salute you in the Lord."
All along, a reader might assume Paul held the pen. He didn't.

teach.b: Once you notice Tertius, the letters start showing their workshop. In Galatians, Paul takes the pen near the end: "Ye see how large a letter I have written unto you with mine own hand."
In Second Thessalonians he calls his handwritten greeting "the token in every epistle." First Peter says it was written "By Silvanus, a faithful brother." Hebrews never names its writer at all.
So a letter could have a sender, a scribe, co-senders in the first line, and a signature at the bottom. Some scholars go a step further.
They ask whether a few letters that carry Paul's or Peter's name were written later by followers, in the teacher's name. Other scholars hold that each letter comes from the one it names.
That's a real debate, and it's still going. Meanwhile, churches kept reading every one of these letters aloud as scripture. Second Peter already talks that way about Paul.
It says his letters hold "some things hard to be understood," which some people twist, "as they do also the other scriptures."
Other scriptures: Paul's mail, set beside the holy books. A letter's place never hung on whose hand held the pen.

how: Churches read the New Testament letters aloud in worship as scripture, often announced by the name the letter carries, as in 'a reading from the letter of Paul to the Romans.'

o: the question of whose hand and name stand behind a letter
a list of the apostles in the order their letters came
a puzzle about which church first got each letter

games.q: the letters' workshop — tap the pairs.
p: wrote Romans down, and said hello
Paul writes with his own hand

s: Paul wrote every word of his letters with his own hand
Romans names its scribe, Tertius; in Galatians Paul takes the pen himself near the end.
it gives no author's name at all, and churches read it as scripture anyway.
2 Peter sets Paul's letters beside 'the other scriptures'
it says some twist Paul's hard sayings, as they do also the other scriptures.

games.q: your church newsletter prints a letter 'from the pastor,' but you know the office manager typed it from his notes. a friend says that makes it fake. what do the New Testament letters suggest?
o: it's fake; only handwritten letters really count.
a letter can have a scribe and still be the sender's.
it belongs to the office manager now.
games.why: Tertius wrote Romans down, 1 Peter was written 'by Silvanus', and Paul signed in his own hand. senders and scribes worked together, and the letters stayed the senders'.

practice: Open any one of the letters to its first verse, on a phone or a page, and look only at the names: who it's from, who it's to, and whether more than one sender stands in that first line. Then rest your eyes on the page for the sit.
Someone wrote this to someone, and it reached you.

wordCard.voice: Who wrote what. The question the letters raise themselves, with a scribe like Tertius, co-senders, and a signature in the writer's own hand.

orig.note: Greek: I write. Paul's "so I write" in 2 Thessalonians 3:17, under his own signature.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: received as scripture, whoever's hand held the pen and whatever name sat at the top. Day fifteen ninety-seven.
